subject.title: iOS app: push notifications for assistant messages + background Talk mode

question: Should native iOS assistant-message notifications send generic alerts only, allow transcript previews behind explicit opt-in, or stay unsupported until a broader mobile notification privacy model is approved?
rationale: The APNs infrastructure and iOS notification command exist, but the permanent payload kind, lock-screen content policy, tap routing, foreground-suppression behavior, and per-node opt-in semantics are privacy-sensitive product choices rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Approve generic chat alerts first
options.body: Add a dedicated chat-reply APNs kind and iOS tap route with generic notification content by default, leaving transcript text for a later explicit opt-in.

options.title: Allow opt-in transcript previews
options.body: Permit assistant reply text in APNs only behind a visible per-device or per-gateway privacy setting with tests and docs for lock-screen behavior.

options.title: Defer native chat pushes
options.body: Keep relying on foreground app state and third-party channels until maintainers define a broader mobile notification policy.

recommendation.title: Approve generic chat alerts first
recommendation.body: Add a dedicated chat-reply APNs kind and iOS tap route with generic notification content by default, leaving transcript text for a later explicit opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans mobile chat UX, background Talk UX, and privacy posture rather than only the existing APNs transport code.
